title: Representation comparison details
legend: **Extended Data Fig. 3 | Representation comparison details.** Participants and conditions as in Fig. 3. **a**, Native heads by route (top) and per-condition gain from adding the retina or clinical data (bottom). #, label encoder inputs may define. **b**, BRAN combined minus 13 arms per condition under one fixed logistic readout (C = 1). Wins and losses, intervals excluding zero. **c**, The 14 arms of that readout. Ticks, one-sided Bonferroni bounds over five prespecified comparators. **d**, BRAN combined minus three arms under four readouts (¶, earlier label-free encoder), and earlier eye-alone AUROC (§, point estimates) beside tuned eye-alone contrasts. **e**, Paired differences with the fixed readout refitted on 25 to 100% of labels. Bars, within-fold participant bootstrap 95% intervals (1,000 draws), unadjusted per condition. BRAN combined did not exceed its clinical route, blood tests plus age or raw clinical values plus age (**c**), losing 7, 6 and 7 conditions to them (**b**). Adding the retina lowered heart-attack detection (**a**). The label-free encoder tied raw concatenation under tuned logistic and lost to ExtraTrees, and the retinal route trailed retinal foundation models (**d**). The clinical route beat BRAN combined at 50% and 75% of labels, and raw clinical values plus age beat it at 75% and scored higher at every budget (**e**). Per-arm tuning turned 125 wins and 0 losses against eight foundation-model arms into 76 and 16 (Fig. 3d). No panel is external validation. The Labrador cache discrepancy reaches 0.0054 AUROC per condition. Intervals for mean rows (**b**) and the 22-condition mean (**a**) are PLACEHOLDER.
methods_notes:
Shared design. Panels b to e use the same five development folds and the same 1,928 people as Fig. 3. The fixed C = 1 readout is a StandardScaler and L2 logistic regression with C = 1, the sealed F1 benchmark. Per-arm tuning and the shared-C readout are in Extended Data Fig. 4a and Extended Data Fig. 4b. Positive differences favour BRAN combined. Bars are 95% within-fold participant bootstrap intervals that condition on the fitted models. All results reuse AI-READI development data, and no panel is external validation. RETFound-Green is not the original RETFound model. The Labrador cache has an unresolved replay discrepancy of up to 0.0054 AUROC per condition. FM, foundation model. MCI, mild cognitive impairment. #, a condition whose definition may use an encoder input, a list that awaits registry confirmation. ¶, the earlier label-free BRAN encoder of d. §, the earlier named eye-alone benchmark of d.
a. Macro AUROC, clinical only 0.6868 [0.6771, 0.6962], combined 0.7026 [0.6931, 0.7118] and retinal only 0.6327 [0.6216, 0.6429], with combined minus clinical only +0.0158 [+0.0102, +0.0214] and combined minus retinal only +0.0699 [+0.0620, +0.0771]. The retina added to clinical data with an interval above zero for 6 conditions (cataracts, glaucoma, macular degeneration, type II diabetes, digestive problems and hearing impairment) and below zero for 1 (heart attack), and clinical data added to the retina with an interval above zero for 20 conditions and below zero for none. The four eye conditions supply 0.278 of the 0.412 summed retinal gain (67.5%). The mean retinal gain over the other 22 conditions is +0.0061 and its interval is PLACEHOLDER. On the bootstrap draws of Extended Data Fig. 4a the mean retinal gain was +0.0695 [+0.0529, +0.0869] over the eye, −0.0022 [−0.0089, +0.0044] over the cardiometabolic and vascular and +0.0160 [+0.0071, +0.0250] over the other conditions, and the mean clinical gain +0.0075 [−0.0058, +0.0208], +0.1163 [+0.1044, +0.1285] and +0.0393 [+0.0298, +0.0492]. In a Holm family of 12 one-sided group tests the retinal gain stayed above zero for the eye and other conditions and the clinical gain for the cardiometabolic and vascular and other conditions. The native heads against raw clinical values plus age gave +0.0327 [+0.0123, +0.0522], +0.0029 [−0.0061, +0.0118] and +0.0127 [+0.0008, +0.0245] and against the tuned BRAN clinical route +0.0509 [+0.0328, +0.0695], −0.0110 [−0.0184, −0.0037] and +0.0099 [+0.0000, +0.0191], supporting a native advantage only in eye conditions (Holm-adjusted p in other conditions 0.108 and 0.130). Both single-modality routes reuse a head trained on both modalities. A hash (#) marks conditions whose definition may use an encoder input. The aggregate withholds the route-matched coverage (matched_population_coverage withheld), so no n is printed for a.
b. Shading runs from grey (arm higher) through white to purple (BRAN combined higher), clipped at 0.10. Column headers leave out the age every arm includes. Wins and losses per arm were clinical route 3 and 7, retinal route 19 and 0, RETFound-Green 19 and 0, DINOv3 18 and 0, VisionFM 21 and 0, RETFound-Green + clinical 13 and 0, DINOv3 + clinical 13 and 0, VisionFM + clinical 16 and 0, Labrador 14 and 0, Labrador + clinical + BRAN eye features 11 and 0, raw clinical + retinal 13 and 0, raw clinical 3 and 7 and blood tests 6 and 6. Against the ten foundation-model, retinal and concatenation comparators BRAN combined has 157 wins and 0 losses in 260 contrasts, and about 17 of the 338 intervals would exclude zero by chance under a global null. The bottom rows are means over the four eye and the 22 other conditions, point estimates only, with intervals PLACEHOLDER. Under per-arm tuning the fixed-readout tally of the eight foundation-model arms, 125 wins and 0 losses, becomes 76 wins and 16 losses (Fig. 3d).
c. BRAN combined scored 0.6750, blood tests plus age 0.6711 [0.6616, 0.6805], and the five arms that join a retinal input to clinical data all scored below blood tests plus age. BRAN combined did not exceed its clinical route (−0.0080 [−0.0157, +0.0001]), blood tests plus age (+0.0039 [−0.0046, +0.0130]) or raw clinical values plus age (0.6839 [0.6747, 0.6938], difference −0.0089 [−0.0179, +0.0001], bound −0.0192). In the arm Labrador + clinical + BRAN eye features + age, the BRAN eye features are the 384 frozen retinal image features that BRAN itself takes as input, stacked with Labrador's embedding of the blood test values, the raw clinical values and typed age. The same 384 BRAN eye features form the retinal block of Raw clinical + retinal + age, so the Labrador arm is exactly that raw concatenation with Labrador's embedding added, and the PCA arms labelled Raw retinal features compress the same 384 features. BRAN's own retinal input features come from a frozen adapted DINOv3-S/16 tower, and the BRAN encoder was also trained on unpaired external sources. These fixed-readout margins shrink under per-arm tuning (Extended Data Fig. 4a and Extended Data Fig. 4b).
d. Rows marked with a pilcrow use an earlier BRAN encoder trained without condition labels, scored on 1,928 matched people with a logistic C tuned on inner folds, a fixed MLP (487 of 780 fits reached the iteration cap) or fixed ExtraTrees. BRAN combined against raw concatenation scored 0.675 against 0.644 with fixed C = 1, 0.693 against 0.689 with tuned C, 0.654 against 0.635 with the MLP and 0.686 against 0.700 with ExtraTrees. With a tuned C the earlier state tied raw concatenation (+0.0036 [−0.0035, +0.0108]), with the MLP it beat it (+0.0190 [+0.0090, +0.0285]), and ExtraTrees on raw concatenation beat it (−0.0140 [−0.0217, −0.0065]). Eye alone in the earlier named benchmark (1,928 people, four penalties), BRAN's retinal route scored 0.6323, below RETFound-Green (0.6385) and DINOv3 (0.6345) and above VisionFM (0.6043), point estimates only. With per-arm tuning on the same people, BRAN retinal route minus each retinal foundation model with age was RETFound-Green −0.0179 [−0.0264, −0.0108], DINOv3 −0.0164 [−0.0240, −0.0087] and VisionFM −0.0212 [−0.0300, −0.0129], with one-sided Bonferroni bounds −0.0306 to −0.0245 in an eye-alone family of three prespecified in the native-heads protocol but not in F1. BRAN's native retinal-route head also had lower point estimates than all three (RETFound-Green −0.0084 [−0.0153, −0.0019], VisionFM −0.0117 [−0.0196, −0.0043] and DINOv3 −0.0068 [−0.0138, +0.0002]). Tuned RETFound-Green with age scored 0.6411. With the current BRAN state and per-arm tuning, BRAN combined minus raw clinical and retinal concatenation was +0.0054 [−0.0011, +0.0122], minus the clinical route −0.0007 [−0.0077, +0.0065] and minus the retinal route +0.0722 [+0.0652, +0.0797] (Extended Data Fig. 4a).
e. Nested 25, 50 and 75% subsets of outer-training people, with 100% taken from c. In absolute macro AUROC BRAN combined scored 0.6443, 0.6598, 0.6673 and 0.6750 at 25, 50, 75 and 100%, above each foundation-model arm with clinical data at every budget (0.5988 to 0.6410) and below raw clinical values plus age at every budget (0.6449, 0.6669, 0.6778 and 0.6839). No label-budget analysis with a tuned readout exists. The BRAN encoder had already used all outer-training labels, so the curves describe the readout label budget and not encoder scaling. Ticks mark one-sided Bonferroni bounds for the five prespecified comparators, exploratory below 100%. The BRAN clinical route beat BRAN combined at 50% (−0.0089 [−0.0167, −0.0011]) and 75% (−0.0096 [−0.0171, −0.0016]), and raw clinical values plus age beat it at 75% (−0.0104 [−0.0197, −0.0012]). Fold n is the smallest per-fold readout pool. Against the ten comparators of b BRAN combined had 123 wins and 1 loss at 25%, 143 wins and 0 losses at 50%, 151 wins and 0 losses at 75% and 157 wins and 0 losses at 100%, and the one loss at 25% was pulmonary problems against Labrador with clinical data and BRAN eye features.
